title: A safety system can identify communication threats before it can monitor them in real time
source_unit: U.S. Government Accountability Office GAO-26-108439 review of FAA spectrum-related threats, eight National Airspace System systems, collaboration practices, and aircraft communication applications
geography: United States National Airspace System and international flight routes using FAA-relevant aviation communications

denominator.unit: spectrum-dependent National Airspace System systems selected by GAO

identified_threats.value: spectrum interference, spoofing, jamming, and other evolving threats

risk_assessment_gap.value: FAA had not completed risk and mitigation assessments and updated security documentation

real_time_monitoring.value: not defined for all spectrum-related threats; incidents may be investigated after reporting

observations.method: GAO analyzed FAA vulnerability assessments, assessed eight spectrum-dependent systems against NIST guidance, reviewed FAA documentation, and interviewed federal and non-federal stakeholders.
observations.uncertainty: The selected systems are not a prevalence estimate for every aviation system, and identified vulnerabilities do not establish that an attack, accident, or operational disruption occurred.
observations.subgroup: Eight selected NAS systems and FAA aviation communication functions; flight crews, passengers, carriers, and airports are not individually observed.
observations.counterinterpretation: Identifying a gap can support preventive action, and the absence of a reported incident does not mean the system failed or was unsafe in a specific flight.

denominator.unit: leading collaboration practices assessed for FAA cybersecurity efforts

external_information_sharing.value: FAA had not established policies or procedures for information sharing, reporting, and coordination with non-federal partners outside existing groups

observations.method: GAO assessed FAA collaboration mechanisms against leading practices and reviewed roles, information sharing, reporting, and coordination with federal and non-federal partners.
observations.uncertainty: The practice score is an organizational assessment, not a measure of every partner interaction or a prediction of incident response quality.
observations.subgroup: FAA, federal partners, aviation-industry stakeholders, and non-federal aviation partners.
observations.counterinterpretation: Existing interagency groups and informal coordination may still support effective action even where formal procedures are incomplete.

denominator.unit: FAA, pilot, and aviation-stakeholder communication applications; no incident or flight denominator

technical_weakness.value: limitations in authentication, encryption, and protocol design can permit interception, spoofing, or message tampering

possible_effect.value: fraudulent clearance cancellations could contribute to delays or safety issues

open_recommendations.unit: GAO recommendations to FAA; all listed as open pending confirmation

observations.method: GAO review of communication-application documentation and FAA vulnerability analysis; possible effects are retained as risk scenarios, not observed outcomes.
observations.uncertainty: The source does not document a malicious transmission, flight delay, accident, passenger harm, or successful mitigation.
observations.subgroup: Aircraft communication applications used by FAA, pilots, and aviation stakeholders.
observations.counterinterpretation: Protocol weaknesses can remain theoretical or be mitigated through operational procedures and other controls; a possible effect is not a realized event.

related_sources.claim: Official full-report version supplies the selected-system assessment, collaboration-practice review, communication vulnerabilities, and recommendations.

boundary: This record establishes identified aviation communication and spectrum-security vulnerabilities plus incomplete monitoring and coordination controls. It does not establish a cyberattack, outage, accident, passenger harm, flight-level risk rate, or failure of a particular aircraft operation.

reproduction_audit.retrieval_hash_scope: Official GAO product page used for the extracted findings; the full report is linked as a related source.
